text:
Transitioning from a PM role to a leadership position means unlearning and adapting how we communicate. I’ve learned the hard way that it’s not just about the details; it’s about the impact. 

I used to drown my audience in process—metrics, steps, and jargon. But what they needed was clarity and outcomes. For instance, instead of saying, "We validated our hypothesis through customer interviews," I should have articulated, "This change will reduce churn and keep our customers happy." 

Owning decisions is crucial too. When a feature slipped, my instinct was to explain the technical debt. But what my leadership team needed was accountability: "I chose to delay this to protect a major release." 

As I dive deeper into AI and product management, I’m realizing that effective communication is about connecting the dots between technical details and business impact. 

Reflect on your own experiences: how can you shift your narrative to resonate more with your audience?

diagram_spec.diagram_prompt: A comparison diagram showing the difference between detail-oriented communication and impact-focused communication.
